question.problem: A thin plate $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=15xy$ is enclosed between the curve $x=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}$ and the $y$-axis  for $0\le y\le 1.$ Find the moment of the plate about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is a type II plane region, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121640/assets/98a791c71bcad80b4e8427f1b2a311e1712fdbc8697d0475b2470c8e0281e8c5.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}},\,0\le y\le 1}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)=15xy.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot 15xy\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}15x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}15x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{y}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}x\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{y}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{15{y}^{2}}{2}(1-{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{15}{2}{y}^{2}-\frac{15}{2}{y}^{4}]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{5}{2}{y}^{3}-\frac{3}{2}{y}^{5}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}-\frac{3}{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
